name: CI

# Verification only - no deployment. Runs on every push and PR so a broken
# main is visible in ~2 minutes instead of at demo time.
on:
  push:
  pull_request:

# A new push supersedes the previous run on the same ref. Without this,
# rapid-fire hackathon pushes queue up and the useful result arrives last.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  frontend:
    name: frontend (lint, types, test, build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      # `npm ci` installs exactly what package-lock.json pins and fails if the
      # lockfile is out of sync with package.json.
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Check formatting
        run: npm run format:check

      - name: Typecheck + build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Test
        run: npm run test

  backend:
    name: backend (lint, format, test)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install uv
        # setup-uv does not publish a floating `v10` tag (its floating
        # majors stop at v7), so this is pinned to an exact release.
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.0.1
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: backend/uv.lock

      # --frozen fails if pyproject.toml and uv.lock have drifted apart,
      # which is exactly the mistake we want CI to catch.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --frozen

      - name: Lint
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Check formatting
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Test
        run: uv run pytest -q

  # Guard the one thing that silently breaks non-Windows teammates.
  line-endings:
    name: line endings
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: setup.sh must be LF, not CRLF
        run: |
          if grep -qU $'\r' setup.sh; then
            echo "::error file=setup.sh::setup.sh contains CRLF line endings and will fail on macOS/Linux with 'bad interpreter: ...^M'"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "setup.sh is LF - ok"
      - name: setup.sh must be valid bash
        run: bash -n setup.sh

## Optional: `codegraph`

Pre-indexed semantic code graph exposed to agents over MCP. Instead of grepping file by
file, the agent queries a graph of symbols and their relationships. Most useful once the
codebase is big enough that navigation costs real time — or when a code-graph UI is itself
on-theme for your track.

```bash
npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph   # or the install.sh / install.ps1 one-liner
codegraph install                  # wires the MCP server
codegraph init                     # index this repo
```

**What we checked** (clone inspected on 2026-08-20):
- MIT licensed. Active — last commit 2026-08-07.
- Fully local: SQLite index, no API keys, no external services, no telemetry endpoints.
- No `postinstall`/`preinstall` hooks in `package.json`.
- Runs a **background daemon** that watches the filesystem and re-indexes on change.
  `CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON=1` disables shared-server mode.
- Bundles its own Node runtime and a Rust parsing kernel — the repo is ~154 MB. The
  published package is smaller, but expect a heavier install than a normal npm CLI.
- `.codegraph/` is gitignored.

**Cost/benefit for a 24-hour build:** the install is the heaviest thing in this document,
and a scaffold this small does not need graph navigation on day one. Add it if you have
slack, or if your track rewards it.

---

## Priority

If time is short, this is the order that actually pays off:

1. **`AGENTS.md` kept accurate** — free, compounding, helps every agent turn.
2. **Supabase MCP** — already wired, zero cost, removes schema guesswork.
3. **`ui-ux-pro-max`** — one command, real payoff when UI is judged.
4. **`codegraph`** — only with slack time.

Do not spend build hours integrating tooling. The scaffold exists so you write product code.

---

## Optional: `entire`

Session tracking for coding agents. Installs git hooks that stamp every commit with an
`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer and push the matching agent session to
`refs/entire/checkpoints/*` on the remote — so a commit can be traced back to the prompts
and turns that produced it. Useful when several people run agents against the same repo
and "why is this line here?" stops being answerable from the diff alone.

```bash
entire enable                 # enable in this repo
entire agent add claude-code  # install the hooks for Claude Code
entire status                 # what is tracked right now
entire doctor                 # diagnose hook / session problems
```

**What we checked** (local setup verified on 2026-08-22, CLI 0.10.2):
- Per-developer, not repo-wide: `.entire/` and `.claude/` are gitignored, so enabling it
  is each person's own call and nobody else's setup changes.
- Hooks installed: `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`,
  `pre-push`. The pre-push hook adds ~1-2s to a push.
- Checkpoints ride along on your normal `git push` as extra refs. They do **not** touch
  branch history — CI and PRs see exactly the commits you made.
- Telemetry is on by default (`.entire/settings.json` → `"telemetry": true`). Turn it off
  there if that matters to you.
